---
title: "Contributing"
---

## Development environment

The repository toolchain is described by `manifest.scm` and used by the Forgejo
`guix` runner:

```bash
guix shell -m manifest.scm
```

The manifest is executable Scheme. Review changes before running it; the
repository `.envrc` uses `require_allowed` to make changed executable inputs
require a fresh direnv approval.

## Build and test

```bash
go build -o wraptool .
go test ./...
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
```

Format changed Go files with `gofmt`. CI also checks that all tracked Go files
are formatted. Do not let Go download a different toolchain silently in
reproducibility checks:

```bash
GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test ./...
```

## Documentation

Install Quarto locally, then preview from the repository root:

```bash
quarto preview docs
```

Build exactly as the Pages workflow does:

```bash
quarto render docs
```

The command writes `docs/_site/`. Generated output and Quarto caches are ignored
and must not be committed to `main`. Use relative links for repository pages and
assets so the site works below the production `/wraptool/` path.

## Documentation accuracy

CLI reference changes should be checked against both Cobra source and live help:

```bash
go run . --help
go run . up --help
go run . init --help
```

Security documentation must distinguish implemented controls from planned work
and list known limitations. Design documents may describe future phases; they
are not automatically statements of current behavior.

## Change workflow

Open issues and pull requests at the [Forgejo
repository](https://forge.snamellit.com/pti/wraptool). Keep changes focused and
include tests beside the Go package they exercise. The project does not currently
publish a private security-reporting channel; do not place secrets or exploit
details in a public issue.
